records.region: Tierra del Fuego, Chile and Argentina; selected cross-border corridor toward Río Grande estuary.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative identity of the mapped receiving river and transboundary system; not a uniform name for the upper Zapata/Grande labeling variants, Donoso and other feeders, side lakes, wetland polygons or every estuarine reach.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected route follows the western Río Zapata / upper Río Grande corridor in Chile, joins the Grande trunk with Japón and separate Lynch–Riveros/Blanco lake-fed contributions, crosses into Argentina, and continues through the lower Grande floodplain to the Atlantic estuary beside Río Grande city and Punta Popper. Río Grande is supported as a representative system identity; varying upper labels and distinct feeders/lakes are retained without a scalar naming claim.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the mapped receiving river and transboundary system; not a uniform name for the upper Zapata/Grande labeling variants, Donoso and other feeders, side lakes, wetland polygons or every estuarine reach.

component_scope_limits: The western approach has Río Zapata on the historical 500k map and Río Grande on the finer MMA hydrography. This source-label variation is preserved, not resolved into a forced whole-feature name.
Río Donoso, Río Japón, Río Riveros and the other tributaries remain distinct branch identities. Unknown feeder or wetland names remain null.
Lago Lynch and Lago Blanco contribute through side outlets but are not selected lake-interior passages. Their names are not propagated to the main river.
The downstream Río Grande label supports a representative receiving-system candidate, not a verified formal registry decision for this model object.
Historical cartography and official historical prose do not establish present perennial flow, exact banks, spring coordinates, tidal shorelines or a surveyed mouth point.
Accepted name, scalar name and Korean name remain null; no application or geometry change is proposed.

component_scope_limits: Gibson Lake is a lake name, not a uniform river or whole-feature scalar name.
Barbour Bay is the actual selected receiving coastal water; Chesterfield Inlet is its broader connected inlet. Neither is substituted as a river name.
The independently mapped Hanway Lake approach is a separate tributary/river entering Barbour Bay from the south.
Unnamed headward streams, lake passages and tributary junctions are kept distinct. No composite system name is invented.
Ordinary component-scale correspondence is sought; no precise bank, vertex, mouth-point, surveyed endpoint, current flow direction or modern legal naming boundary is claimed.
Pixel coverage and retained model continuity do not establish a missing geographic connector.

records.region: Northern Nunavik, Quebec, Canada; Torngat headwater setting through the Koroc valley to the Ungava coastal estuary.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected system corresponds to the Rivière Koroc corridor: an unnamed Torngat headward lake/stream setting connects to the Koroc valley, passes its mapped tributary joins and reaches the lower estuary opening toward Ungava Bay. ARK2005 original basin/drainage maps cover all selected components. Rivière Koroc is supported as a representative system identity; every accepted, scalar and Korean name remains null and product application remains false. Optional later-plan/index availability failures do not leave a geographic gap.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
